business_problem: Pictet wanted more than chat-based assistance: it needed agentic AI that could automate internal engineering, compliance, and business workflows inside a Swiss private bank without breaking data residency, risk, or training obligations.
solution_summary: Pictet rolled out Claude Code and Claude Cowork through a staged, persona-based program that began in its 1,500-person technology division and expanded across product and business teams. Artefact ran 25 hands-on workshops to help teams build with the tools rather than just query them. To satisfy banking controls, Pictet put business use cases behind a purpose-built API gateway that keeps processing in the EU or Switzerland and prevents data from persisting for model training. Early MCP connections expose internal systems such as GitHub, Jira, Figma, and the internal wiki, letting Claude participate in engineering, compliance, prototyping, and operational workflows. The same setup supports concrete jobs such as comparing more than 50 directives to current regulations, building alerting systems, creating custom thin-client UIs, and automating weekly marketwatch reports.

business_outcome: Pictet has given roughly 700 people access to Claude Code and Claude Cowork, trained more than 500 staff, reduced some prototype work from two weeks to two hours, and brought compliance, infrastructure, and business automation tasks into workflows that fit the bank's risk framework.
